narrative:
Material PL1__MA79AD09 exhibits intermittent demand with a coefficient of variation of 0.51. 
The analysis reveals significant variability in both demand (CV=0.51) and lead time (CV=0.52), 
necessitating a substantial safety stock buffer of 13,741 units to achieve the 95.0% service level target. 

The current SAP policy maintains only 3,943 units of safety stock with a 1,171-unit order quantity, 
resulting in extremely high ordering costs of $90,830.64 per year due to frequent small orders. 
The optimized policy balances ordering and holding costs through an EOQ-based order quantity of 36,774 units, 
achieving annual cost savings of $83,596.79 (91.3% reduction).

The decreasing demand trend and highly_variable distribution pattern require continuous monitoring. 
Lead time variability (mean=2.38 days, std=1.25 days) contributes significantly to safety stock requirements, 
accounting for 49,918,538 units of variance versus 19,868,264 from demand variability.
